doc.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Family life and travel
summary: Touring is hard with his son and daughter; he wants more time off.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah. You’ve got a family now, and do you find the traveling a little harder?

Yeah. Especially with my son. I’m divorced from obviously my first wife. And I have a daughter by my second wife now. And so I see my son when I’m in town. And everything, there’s always something going on when I’m in town so it’s very hard to try and make time and go and do. And luckily he lives a block and a half from me, which only happened in the last two years, so you’re able to leave the room, walk down and there he is. So that’s the other reason why less gigs more money is a priority. You know I’d like to see that part, to be able to at least say let’s take off July, or two weeks in July and be able to know that — my kids are off in the summer. And then have a week off at Christmas. You know I like working and I know that’s what you’ve got to do. So to be able to plot it out better is the key.
